item.title: In Pictures: Hong Kong protesters call for ceasefire ahead of Russia-Ukraine war’s 4th anniversary
item.description: Five Hong Kong protesters staged a demonstration on Saturday, three days before Russia’s full-blown war in Ukraine enters its fifth year, calling for a ceasefire and an end to the conflict. item.title: Court rejects appeals of all 12 activists in landmark ‘Hong Kong 47’ national security case
item.description: A Hong Kong court has dismissed the appeals of all 12 activists who challenged their convictions or jail terms in the city’s landmark national security case. item.title: Hong Kong gov’t mulls booking system, fees for tourist camping spots after NGO slams inaction on overcrowding
item.description: Hong Kong authorities will consult lawmakers on introducing booking systems and fees for popular tourist camping spots to combat overcrowding, following NGO criticism of government inaction. item.description: China urged the United States on Monday to cancel unilateral tariffs announced by President Donald Trump after the US Supreme Court struck down many of his measures. item.description: By John Weaver Eileen Gu soared to victory in the women’s freeski halfpipe final on Sunday to end her wait for a gold medal at the Milan-Cortina Olympics, becoming the most decorated freestyle skier in the history of the Winter Games. item.title: Hong Kong privacy watchdog joins 60 overseas authorities warning of AI-generated intimate images
item.description: Hong Kong’s privacy watchdog has joined 60 other overseas authorities in warning against non-consensual AI-generated images depicting individuals, including children and other vulnerable groups. Hong Kong’s Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD) issued a joint statement on Monday, alongside dozens of other privacy and data protection authorities. item.title: Hong Kong man charged with loitering after allegedly splashing unknown liquid on 3 women
item.description: A 34-year-old man has been charged with loitering after allegedly splashing an unknown liquid on three women in separate incidents in Sha Tin. The defendant, a chef surnamed Cheung, appeared at the Shatin Magistrates’ Courts on Monday. He was denied bail, and his case was adjourned to April 10, local media reported. item.title: Panama wrests control of 2 canal ports from Hong Kong’s CK Hutchison
item.description: Panamanian authorities took control Monday of two ports on the Panama Canal from CK Hutchison after the Hong Kong-based conglomerate’s concession was annulled amid a row between the United States and China.
